This highlights severe security vulnerabilities in integrated AI writing assistants.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase, as validated by the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.

It utilizes local AI coding agents, ensuring all processing runs directly on the user's device.
The core value proposition is providing private, on-device AI assistance for coding tasks.

stories.title: OpenAI president says it’s ‘building a family of devices’ for its AI chatbots
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: OpenAI is developing a 'family of devices' to enhance interaction with its AI chatbots.
The announcement suggests a move beyond purely software-based AI experiences.
The company did not confirm rumors regarding a specific smart speaker launch timeline (e.g., 2027).

stories.title: DoorDash is going airborne with new drone delivery division
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: DoorDash is launching a new drone delivery division named DoorDash Air.
The company has secured necessary approval from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).
This move signals a significant industry shift toward autonomous aerial delivery in food service.

stories.title: Anthropic is finding bugs faster than Microsoft can fix them
stories.author: Renee Dudley, ProPublica
bullet_points: Anthropic is reportedly discovering security vulnerabilities in its models at a faster rate than Microsoft can patch them.
The news highlights a significant and ongoing security challenge within the rapidly evolving AI landscape.
Microsoft is reportedly engaged in an urgent, behind-the-scenes effort to address these emerging exploits.

stories.title: Google's SynthID watermark is hard to break, but it doesn't solve AI disinformation
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google's SynthID watermark technology shows promise in making AI-generated content harder to tamper with.
The article argues that watermarking alone is insufficient to solve the broader problem of AI disinformation.
The future of discerning authentic content online is predicted to be a significant and complex challenge.

stories.title: Detecting Knowledge Inconsistencies Across Text, Tables, and Knowledge Graphs
stories.author: Raphaël Troncy
bullet_points: Addresses the critical problem of detecting knowledge inconsistencies when information is spread across different modalities (text, tables, knowledge graphs).
Focuses on 'modality-level inconsistency detection,' a key challenge for reliable LLM applications like RAG.
Proposes a taxonomy to categorize and study these cross-modal knowledge conflicts, relevant to improving knowledge base integrity.

stories.title: Show HN: Open-source engine running Gemma 4 26B in 2 GB RAM on any M-series Mac
stories.author: gitpusher42
bullet_points: A new open-source inference engine, TurboFieldfare, allows running large language models on consumer hardware.
The engine enables running the 4-bit quantized Gemma 4 26B model using only ~2 GB of RAM on M-series Macs.
The project highlights the trend of pushing on-device AI capabilities by optimizing memory usage for large models.

stories.title: Slopsquatting: The Supply Chain Attack That Weaponizes AI Hallucinations
stories.author: nazar-boyko
bullet_points: Introduces 'Slopsquatting,' a novel supply chain attack vector targeting AI systems.
This attack leverages the tendency of AI models to 'hallucinate' (invent false information).
It is positioned as an evolution of traditional typo-squatting, targeting AI assistants.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across diverse hardware.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting Apple silicon users with broader model access.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of 'subagents' for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added to enhance the knowledge base and real-time data access of Claude Code.

stories.title: Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 feels like the future
stories.author: Dominic Preston
bullet_points: Samsung is positioning the Galaxy Z Fold 8 as the standard, mainstream design for future foldable phones.
The device is being marketed as the 'new normal' rather than a niche, experimental product.
There is speculation that Apple may also view this foldable form factor as a significant future direction.

stories.title: Artists are lawyering up against AI slop, and some are even winning
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Artists are actively challenging the use of their work in training AI models.
The issue was highlighted by a searchable dataset of training materials published by The Atlantic.
Legal action is emerging, with some artists reportedly achieving success in their disputes against AI misuse.

stories.title: Google begins global rollout of age verification API in Google Play
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google is globally rolling out a new Age Verification API within Google Play.
The API's implementation relies on parental controls managed through Google Family Link.
This signals a growing industry focus on child safety and age-appropriate content filtering.

stories.title: Elon Musk’s xAI is trying to sue its way out of a Grok reckoning
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: xAI, Elon Musk's AI venture, is reportedly engaging in legal action regarding Grok.
The core of the legal challenge involves contesting a ban on a 'nudifying app' in Minnesota.
Musk is framing the local app ban as a constitutional violation.

stories.title: New AMD Linux patch boosts low-end gaming performance on Steam Deck
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: AMD released a new Linux patch specifically targeting the Steam Deck.
The update improves performance in EPP mode, which is relevant for low-end hardware.
Users can expect a significant boost, specifically a ~32% increase in '1% low' frame rates for gaming.

stories.title: What happens when you put AI to work deciphering lost languages?
stories.author: Jane Adkins, The Conversation
bullet_points: AI is being applied to the challenging task of deciphering lost languages.
The article suggests that while AI excels at pattern recognition, human expertise remains crucial.
This represents an intersection of advanced AI capabilities and historical/linguistic research.

stories.title: Elon Musk finally launches X Money. What could possibly go wrong?
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Elon Musk has initiated the launch of 'X Money'.
The rollout is expected to encounter issues, specifically excluding major US financial markets.
The article suggests potential problems associated with the new financial offering.

stories.title: Pass the Baton: Trajectory-Relayed On-Policy Distillation
stories.author: Yongliang Shen
bullet_points: The paper addresses a critical issue in On-Policy Distillation (OPD) known as 'prefix failure'.
Prefix failure occurs when a student model commits to an incorrect reasoning path, leading to unreliable supervision.
The research identifies a 'teacher-student continuation asymmetry' on failed prefixes, suggesting a mechanism for improvement.

stories.title: $π\mathbf{R}^2$: Reactive Real-time Flow Policies
stories.author: Shubham Tulsiani
bullet_points: Current generalist manipulation policies often use action-chunking flow policies based on large backbones.
These chunked policies are open-loop, meaning they lack real-time reactivity to mid-execution sensory input.
The high latency of the perception-to-action pipeline prevents frequent replanning, leading to stale committed actions.

stories.title: Desktop-Delta Bench: Do Computer-Use Models Understand Desktop GUI Transitions?
stories.author: Yuan Chen
bullet_points: New benchmark, Desktop-Delta Bench, addresses a gap in evaluating Computer-Use Agents (CUAs) operating via desktop GUIs.
Current evaluation methods fail to test if models understand the causal, task-relevant transitions between GUI states.
The benchmark specifically tackles the challenge of asynchronous interactions (inference, rendering, capture) crucial for robust agent behavior.

stories.title: Falling Behind Drives Unsafe Development in an Idealised AI Race Experiment
stories.author: The Anh Han
bullet_points: The study investigates the tension between speed and safety in technological development, specifically within AI.
It posits that competitive pressure in AI races can incentivize riskier, less safety-conscious development.
The findings are based on a framed behavioral experiment simulating an idealized AI race.

stories.title: CHARM: A Multimodal Graph Foundation Model with Hierarchical Context Modeling for Zero-Shot Transfer
stories.author: Dongxiao He
bullet_points: Introduces CHARM, a new Multimodal Graph Foundation Model (GFM).
Addresses the challenge of zero-shot knowledge transfer in complex, real-world multimodal graphs (text, images, etc.).
Focuses on hierarchical context modeling to enable effective transfer without extensive domain-specific labeling.

stories.title: MDTransformer: A Hardware-Software Co-Design of Mode-Division Photonic Transformer Accelerator with Inverse-Designed Coherent Crossbar
stories.author: Mahmoud Rasras
bullet_points: Introduces MDTransformer, a novel hardware-software co-design for Photonic Transformer Accelerators (PTAs).
Aims to overcome limitations in current PTAs, specifically the inefficiency and cost associated with multi-wavelength light generation and active phase-shifters.
Focuses on improving the practicality and efficiency of accelerating Transformer inference using photonic computing.

stories.title: Pictura: Perspective-View Self-Play at Scale for Driving
stories.author: Matthieu Cord
bullet_points: The research introduces 'Pictura,' a method using self-play in simulation to generate robust driving policies at scale.
The current approach relies on privileged, complete observations (like exact poses), creating a 'representation gap' when deployed with real-world, partial camera views.
A common mitigation strategy—distilling the privileged policy into a camera-input student—is noted but leaves the student's imitation capabilities incomplete.

stories.title: Empirical Evaluation of Out-Of-Distribution Performance of Tabular Foundation Models
stories.author: Felipe Grijalva
bullet_points: The research evaluates Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs), which show competitive performance against traditional tree-based models for tabular data.
A key focus is assessing TFM robustness under distribution shifts, a critical issue in real-world applications where IID assumptions fail.
The paper provides an empirical evaluation of how well these models perform when encountering Out-Of-Distribution (OOD) data.

stories.title: Does Runtime Topology Context Improve LLM-Generated Kubernetes Security Patches?
stories.author: Farooq Shaikh
bullet_points: The research investigates using Runtime Topology Context to enhance LLM-generated security patches for Kubernetes.
Current LLM-based security remediation systems often fail because they process KSPM findings in isolation, lacking context from the live service call graph.
The study addresses the limitation where general hardening knowledge is insufficient for complex, context-aware security fixes in cloud-native environments.

stories.title: MemLens: A Value-Aware Memory Management System with Interactive Analytics for LLM-based Agents
stories.author: Lizhen Cui
bullet_points: MemLens introduces a value-aware memory management system specifically designed for LLM-based agents.
It addresses a limitation in current systems where memory records are treated uniformly, leading to storage of redundant or low-impact data.
The system aims to improve long-horizon reasoning and knowledge reuse by intelligently managing heterogeneous user-LLM interaction records.

stories.title: $π\mathbf{R}^2$: Reactive Real-time Flow Policies
stories.author: Shubham Tulsiani
bullet_points: Current generalist manipulation policies rely on action-chunking flow policies built on large backbones.
These chunked policies suffer from a lack of reactivity because they run open-loop, unable to react to mid-execution sensory input.
The high latency of the perception-to-action pipeline prevents frequent replanning, leading to stale committed actions.

stories.title: Spend Experts Where You Are Unsure: Confidence-Adaptive Routing for Mixture-of-Experts LoRA
stories.author: Daniel Whitmore
bullet_points: Introduces CARE (Confidence-Adaptive Routing of Experts) to improve Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LoRA.
Addresses the limitation of fixed expert routing by using the router's output distribution as a per-token uncertainty signal.
Aims to optimize resource allocation by directing tokens to experts based on model confidence, preventing over-spending on easy tokens.

stories.title: VetClaw: An Edge-Cloud Multimodal Agentic System for Veterinary Disease Screening
stories.author: Abdur R. Shahid
bullet_points: VetClaw is an edge-cloud multimodal agentic system designed for early veterinary disease screening.
It utilizes an edge camera module for image capture, sending data to a server-hosted vision-language model for zero-shot classification.
The architecture separates concerns: OpenClaw handles edge orchestration (scheduling, interaction), while LangGraph manages the core agent logic.

stories.title: Reinformed Dreamer: An Asymmetric World Model Efficiently Trained through Latent Guidance
stories.author: Damien Ernst
bullet_points: Introduces 'Reinformed Dreamer,' a new approach to world modeling in reinforcement learning.
Proposes using 'latent guidance' as an additional form of supervision beyond standard rewards.
Aims to improve representation learning and behavior in reinforcement learning, especially under partial observability.

stories.title: Parallel Decoding Distillation for Fast Image and Video Generation
stories.author: Julius Berner
bullet_points: Addresses the computational expense of iterative sampling in video diffusion/flow models.
Critiques current acceleration methods (like VSD) for being hard to optimize and causing mode collapse/loss of diversity.
Proposes 'Parallel Decoding Distillation' as a new approach to improve speed and maintain video quality/motion.

stories.title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization and Muon: Robustness under the Spectral Norm
stories.author: Michael Murray
bullet_points: The paper addresses the geometric dependency in Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM), a technique used to improve model generalization.
It introduces the Muon optimizer, which incorporates matrix-aware optimization to handle the structure of parameter perturbations.
The research focuses on enhancing model robustness by considering the spectral norm when defining 'small' perturbations.

stories.title: Empirical Evaluation of Out-Of-Distribution Performance of Tabular Foundation Models
stories.author: Felipe Grijalva
bullet_points: The paper evaluates Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs), which are showing competitive performance against traditional ensemble tree-based models for tabular data.
A key focus is the robustness of TFMs when facing real-world distribution shifts, a scenario often ignored in standard IID training.
The research provides an empirical evaluation of how well these models perform when tested on Out-Of-Distribution (OOD) data.

stories.title: Untangling Co-Drift: Proactive Multi-Intent Failure Prediction and Root-Cause Disambiguation for Self-Driving Networks
stories.author: Walid Aljoby
bullet_points: Addresses a critical challenge in self-driving networks: predicting and disambiguating failures caused by 'co-drift' between monitoring, analytics, and actuation functions.
Formalizes network health by treating core functions (telemetry, analytics, actuation) as distinct, continuously satisfiable operational 'intents'.
Focuses on proactive failure prediction and root-cause analysis, which is crucial for achieving highly autonomous, self-monitoring systems.

stories.title: Instruction-Tuned Models Locally Reuse Human Syntax More Than Humans Do
stories.author: Zandi Eberstadt
bullet_points: The research investigates whether instruction-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit syntactic convergence towards human users.
Syntactic convergence is a known human phenomenon where speakers adapt their language to match their interlocutor's grammar.
The study uses substitution-paradigm data to compare model behavior against human baselines across various syntactic constructions.

stories.title: Polistemics: Evaluating LLMs as Information Mediators in Politics & Elections
stories.author: Baran Peters
bullet_points: Introduces 'Polistemics,' a new benchmark for evaluating how Large Language Models (LLMs) mediate political information.
Addresses a gap in current research by focusing on LLMs as 'mediators' rather than just information 'reproducers' in political contexts.
Grounds the evaluation in 'Epistemic Modesty,' a normative framework to assess responsible information mediation.

stories.title: A Cost-Effective Multimodal LLM Reasoning Framework for Question Answering over Irregular Clinical Time Series
stories.author: Jindong Han
bullet_points: Addresses a critical gap in current multimodal LLMs: handling the sparsity and asynchrony of irregular clinical time series (ICTS).
Introduces ClinPRISM, a proposed cost-effective multimodal LLM reasoning framework specifically designed for clinical QA.
Focuses on a high-impact domain (healthcare/clinical applications) where accurate time-series analysis is crucial.

stories.title: Evaluating Multi-Turn Multimodal Diagnostic Reasoning on Challenging Real-World Clinical Cases
stories.author: Yifan Peng
bullet_points: The paper addresses a gap in current evaluations of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in clinical settings.
It argues that real-world clinical diagnosis requires assessing dynamic reasoning, including progressive information disclosure and hypothesis updating, not just single-turn accuracy.
The research aims to develop more realistic evaluation benchmarks to capture the complexity of clinical practice for MLLMs.

stories.title: Minimizing Targeted Activations: Input-Only Suppression of Evaluation-Awareness Latents in Large Language Models
stories.author: Dipesh Mahato
bullet_points: The research proposes an input-only method to suppress specific internal model activations (evaluation-awareness latents) in LLMs.
This technique aims to prevent models from altering their behavior when they detect they are being evaluated, thereby maintaining the validity of safety testing.
It adapts existing steering methods (like Fluent Dreaming/EPO) to operate entirely at the prompt/input level without requiring inference-time model access.

stories.title: RSIBench-Data: Benchmarking Data-Centric Research for Recursive Self-Improvement
stories.author: Michael Qizhe Shieh
bullet_points: Introduces RSIBench-Data, a new benchmark designed to evaluate data-centric research for recursive self-improvement in LLMs.
Addresses the challenge of current benchmarks mixing research decisions with system implementation, which obscures agent capabilities.
Focuses on automating the loop where model failures are converted into improvements through data-centric post-training strategies.

stories.title: AI's Capability in Assisting Scientific Research in Physics, Astrophysics, and Cosmology II: Project Planning and Proposal Evaluation
stories.author: Mingshen Zhou
bullet_points: The study evaluates the capability of LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, DeepSeek) in assisting scientific project planning and proposal evaluation in physics/astrophysics.
Human-generated and LLM-generated one-page research proposals were blindly evaluated by human and advanced LLM reviewers.
This research explores the practical utility and reliability of current frontier LLMs in high-level scientific research support.

stories.title: Keychron announces first open-source firmware for gaming mice
stories.author: JLO64
bullet_points: Keychron is releasing open-source firmware for its gaming mice.
This move promotes transparency and customization within the peripheral hardware space.
It represents a shift towards more open ecosystems in consumer gaming gear.

stories.title: A.I. companies are recruiting electricians and carpenters by the thousands
stories.author: thm
bullet_points: AI companies are reportedly hiring large numbers of skilled tradespeople.
The recruitment focus is specifically on electricians and carpenters.
This suggests a growing need for physical infrastructure support for AI development.
